#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# healthcheck.sh — Check whether local services are responding.
#
# Checks the configured ports and reports their status. Intended for
# use in monitoring, CI smoke tests, or quick manual verification.

set -uo pipefail

# --- Configuration ---------------------------------------------------------

HOST="${HEALTHCHECK_HOST:-localhost}"
# Ports to check. Override with: PORTS="3000 8080 9090" ./healthcheck.sh
PORTS="${PORTS:-3000 8080}"
# Per-request timeout in seconds.
TIMEOUT="${HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT:-3}"

# --- Colors (disabled if not a terminal) -----------------------------------

if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
  GREEN=$'\033[0;32m'; RED=$'\033[0;31m'; BOLD=$'\033[1m'; RESET=$'\033[0m'
else
  GREEN=""; RED=""; BOLD=""; RESET=""
fi

# --- Check function ---------------------------------------------------------

# Returns 0 if the port responds, 1 otherwise.
check_port() {
  local host="$1" port="$2"

  # Prefer curl for an HTTP-aware check; fall back to a raw TCP connect.
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    local code
    code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
                 --max-time "$TIMEOUT" \
                 "http://${host}:${port}/" 2>/dev/null)"
    # Any HTTP response (even 404) means the service is up and listening.
    if [[ -n "$code" && "$code" != "000" ]]; then
      echo "$code"
      return 0
    fi
    return 1
  elif command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if nc -z -w "$TIMEOUT" "$host" "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "tcp"
      return 0
    fi
    return 1
  else
    # Last resort: bash's built-in /dev/tcp.
    if timeout "$TIMEOUT" bash -c ">/dev/tcp/${host}/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "tcp"
      return 0
    fi
    return 1
  fi
}

# --- Main -------------------------------------------------------------------

echo "${BOLD}Health check @ ${HOST}${RESET}"
echo "-----------------------------------"

failures=0
for port in $PORTS; do
  if result="$(check_port "$HOST" "$port")"; then
    printf '  %-6s %sUP%s   (%s)\n' "$port" "$GREEN" "$RESET" "$result"
  else
    printf '  %-6s %sDOWN%s\n' "$port" "$RED" "$RESET"
    failures=$((failures + 1))
  fi
done

echo "-----------------------------------"
if [[ "$failures" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "${GREEN}All services healthy.${RESET}"
  exit 0
else
  echo "${RED}${failures} service(s) not responding.${RESET}"
  exit 1
fi

# healthcheck.sh — Check whether our services are responding.
#
# Checks TCP connectivity and (when possible) HTTP responsiveness for the

  "web-app:localhost:3000"
  "api:localhost:8080"

  local host="$1" port="$2"

  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Try HTTP first; treat any HTTP response as "responding".
    if curl --silent --output /dev/null --max-time "$TIMEOUT" \

    nc -z -w "$TIMEOUT" "$host" "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    return 1
  fi

  # Last resort: bash /dev/tcp

    exec 3>&- 3<&-
    return 0
  fi

  return 1

  echo "-------------------------------------------"

      overall=1
    fi
  done

  echo "-------------------------------------------"
  if [ "$overall" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "${GREEN}All services healthy.${RESET}"
  else
    echo "${YELLOW}One or more services are not responding.${RESET}"
  fi

  return "$overall"
}

#
# healthcheck.sh - Check whether local services are responding.
#
# Probes a set of host:port endpoints and reports their status.
# Exits 0 if all services are healthy, 1 if any are down.

set -u

# Services to check, formatted as "name=host:port[/path]"
SERVICES=(
  "web=localhost:3000/health"
  "api=localhost:8080"
)

# How long to wait for each service (seconds)
TIMEOUT="${HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT:-3}"

# --- colors (disabled if not a TTY) ---
if [ -t 1 ]; then
  GREEN=$'\033[0;32m'; RED=$'\033[0;31m'; BOLD=$'\033[1m'; RESET=$'\033[0m'
else
  GREEN=""; RED=""; BOLD=""; RESET=""
fi

# Check a single endpoint. Returns 0 if it responds, 1 otherwise.
check_endpoint() {
  local host="$1" port="$2" path="$3"
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # --fail makes HTTP >= 400 count as failure; -s/-o keep it quiet.
    curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time "$TIMEOUT" "http://${host}:${port}${path}"
    return $?
  elif command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    nc -z -w "$TIMEOUT" "$host" "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1

  else

    return $?
  fi
}

echo "${BOLD}Service health check${RESET} ($(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'))"
echo "-------------------------------------------"

failures=0
for entry in "${SERVICES[@]}"; do
  name="${entry%%=*}"
  target="${entry#*=}"

  # Split target into host:port and optional /path
  hostport="${target%%/*}"
  if [ "$target" = "$hostport" ]; then
    path=""
  else
    path="/${target#*/}"
  fi
  host="${hostport%%:*}"
  port="${hostport##*:}"

  if check_endpoint "$host" "$port" "$path"; then
    printf "  %-6s %s%s%s  (%s:%s%s)\n" \

  else
    printf "  %-6s %s%s%s  (%s:%s%s)\n" \
      "$name" "$RED" "DOWN" "$RESET" "$host" "$port" "$path"
    failures=$((failures + 1))
  fi
done

echo "-------------------------------------------"
if [ "$failures" -eq 0 ]; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# healthcheck.sh — Check whether local services are responding.
#
# Probes a set of TCP ports (default: 3000 and 8080) and reports the
# status of each. Exits 0 if all services are healthy, 1 otherwise.
#
# Usage:
#   ./healthcheck.sh                 # check default ports 3000 and 8080
#   ./healthcheck.sh 3000 8080 9090  # check a custom list of ports
#   HOST=example.internal ./healthcheck.sh
#

set -uo pipefail

HOST="${HOST:-localhost}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3}"   # seconds per probe

  PORTS=("$@")
else
  PORTS=(3000 8080)
fi

# Colors (only if stdout is a terminal).
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
  GREEN=$'\033[0;32m'; RED=$'\033[0;31m'; BOLD=$'\033[1m'; RESET=$'\033[0m'
else
  GREEN=''; RED=''; BOLD=''; RESET=''
fi

# Probe a single port. Returns 0 if something accepts the connection.
check_port() {
  local host="$1" port="$2"

  # Prefer curl for an HTTP-aware check, fall back to nc, then to bash's
  # built-in /dev/tcp if neither tool is available.

    nc -z -w "$TIMEOUT" "$host" "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1
  else
    timeout "$TIMEOUT" bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${host}/${port}" 2>/dev/null
  fi
}

echo "-----------------------------------------------"

overall_status=0
for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
  if check_port "$HOST" "$port"; then
    printf "  port %-5s : %sUP%s\n"   "$port" "$GREEN" "$RESET"
  else
    printf "  port %-5s : %sDOWN%s\n" "$port" "$RED" "$RESET"
    overall_status=1
  fi
done

  echo "${GREEN}All services healthy.${RESET}"
else

fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# healthcheck.sh - Check whether local services are responding.
#
# Checks that the configured service ports accept connections (and,
# where an HTTP health endpoint exists, that it responds successfully).
# Exits 0 if all services are healthy, 1 if any are down.

set -uo pipefail

# Host and ports to check. Override HOST via env var if needed.
HOST="${HOST:-localhost}"

# Format: "port:label:health_path"  (health_path optional)
SERVICES=(
  "3000:api:/health"
  "8080:web:"
)

# Connection timeout in seconds.
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3}"

overall_status=0

# Check raw TCP connectivity to a port.
check_port() {
  local host="$1" port="$2"

  if command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    nc -z -w "$TIMEOUT" "$host" "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1
    return $?
  fi

  # Fallback: use bash's built-in /dev/tcp.
  timeout "$TIMEOUT" bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/${host}/${port}" >/dev/null 2>&1
  return $?
}

# Check an HTTP endpoint, returns 0 if it responds with a 2xx/3xx status.
check_http() {
  local url="$1"

  if ! command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 2  # curl unavailable; caller should fall back to port check
  fi

  local code
  code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time "$TIMEOUT" "$url" 2>/dev/null)"

  if [[ "$code" =~ ^[23][0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

echo "Health check @ $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo "Host: $HOST"
echo "-----------------------------------------"

for entry in "${SERVICES[@]}"; do
  IFS=':' read -r port label health_path <<< "$entry"

  status="DOWN"
  detail=""

  if check_port "$HOST" "$port"; then
    status="UP"

    # If a health path is defined, verify the HTTP endpoint too.
    if [[ -n "${health_path:-}" ]]; then
      url="http://${HOST}:${port}${health_path}"
      if check_http "$url"; then
        detail="(HTTP ${health_path} OK)"
      else
        rc=$?
        if [[ $rc -eq 2 ]]; then
          detail="(port open; curl unavailable, skipped HTTP check)"
        else
          status="UNHEALTHY"
          detail="(port open but ${health_path} failed)"
        fi
      fi
    fi
  fi

  case "$status" in
    UP)        symbol="✓" ;;
    UNHEALTHY) symbol="!" ; overall_status=1 ;;
    *)         symbol="✗" ; overall_status=1 ;;
  esac

  printf '%s  %-6s port %-5s : %-9s %s\n' \
    "$symbol" "$label" "$port" "$status" "$detail"
done

echo "-----------------------------------------"
if [[ "$overall_status" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "All services healthy."
else
  echo "One or more services are not healthy."
fi

exit "$overall_status"
